name: Rewound Reel
text: Whenever you lead a club, you may have the lowest club win that trick instead of the highest.
decision: Whether to reverse each club you lead: lead a low club and reverse it to win cheaply, or, on a nil, lead a high club and reverse it to lose safely.
opponent: Announced as you lead, before anyone follows; opponents answer by trumping club leads or keeping their low clubs.
aiNote: Reverse a club you lead if you bid nil and it is a 10 or higher, or if you did not bid nil and it is a 6 or lower.
rationale: The owner decides lead by lead, knowing their own hand, so the reversal always serves them: a nil sheds a high club on its own lead, and a contract hand wins a trick with a two while saving its high cards. Trumps still beat clubs, and ties still go to the later card. It acts only on your own club leads, about two a round for a hand built around it.
deviation: Revision 1: replaced a global rule that reversed every trick led with clubs, which helped every seat about equally.
